title: automation: tenant RBAC bootstrap for private-installer (helm + terraform)
author: Priya Nambiar
release_notes: Add automation for tenant RBAC bootstrap used by Private (VPC/on-prem) installer: Helm chart templating + Terraform module wiring. Enables unattended tenant creation with least-privilege roles and audit-ready bindings.
description: Motivation: Private deployments require a deterministic, auditable bootstrap flow to create tenant-specific RBAC roles, service accounts, and scoped bindings during installer runs (helm + terraform). This PR automates the RBAC artifacts and wiring so the private-installer can perform tenant bootstrap without interactive steps. Changes: - Add Helm templates for tenant rolebindings and ClusterRole templates used by the private-installer. Templates support configurable prefixing, namespace isolation, and optional KMS-scoped service accounts. - Add Terraform module (terraform/modules/tenant-bootstrap) that wraps Helm release and exposes outputs for status and role-principal ARNs. - Provide automation scripts used by the installer to render and apply RBAC during the initial bootstrap and during in-place upgrades/rollbacks. - Introduce policy.yaml examples and test fixtures used by the installer e2e harness. Checklist: - [x] Helm templates and tests - [x] Terraform module + plan validation - [x] Integration smoke test in private-installer E2E - [x] Security review + least-privilege validation - [x] Documentation for operator-run/automation-run flows Notes on behavior: - The default templates create namespaced roles with minimal permissions required for tenant runtime operations (read/write to tenant namespace resources, access limited CRDs). - A ClusterRole is only created when the installer is run in cluster-scoped mode; otherwise all bindings remain namespaced. - Service accounts used by automation are annotated for KMS/HSM key access only when the installer flag enable_kms is true. Testing and CI: - Local helm-lint + template rendering unit tests added. - Terraform plan is validated in CI (changes gated). - E2E private-installer pipeline runs a smoke test that exercises tenant bootstrap and rollback. Migration/Upgrade notes: - When upgrading, the installer will perform a dry-run plan and create any missing roles/bindings. It will not remove existing bindings unless --prune-rbac is explicitly passed. - Rollback path restores previous helm release revisions and applies terraform state rollback where applicable. Security considerations: - Audit logging is enabled on created service accounts via annotations and optional KMS policies. - RBAC diffs are recorded in installer logs and uploaded to the designated audit bucket when configured. Related work: ENG-1458 (tenant bootstrap), ENG-1472 (private-installer upgrade tooling), SUP-724 (customer support request for unattended tenant creation).

review_comments: Michael Chen (reviewer): Can we avoid creating a ClusterRole by default? Suggest defaulting to namespaced-only to reduce blast radius.
Author (Priya): Agree. Changed templates to require cluster_scoped: true to emit ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding. Updated docs and tests.
Sofia Alvarez (reviewer): Terraform module needs clearer outputs for Helm release name and rendered manifest; also add a prevents-drift check.
Author (Priya): Added outputs.release_name and outputs.rendered_manifest. Added a lightweight drift check script that runs during e2e smoke tests.
Diego Ramos (security): Add annotations for audit logging and KMS key binding; ensure service account permissions are minimal.
Author (Priya): Added annotations and gating via enable_kms flag. Verified least-privilege with internal policy lint.
Michael Chen (approval): LGTM after minor comments addressed. Approving for merge.
merge_summary: Squash and merge performed by Michael Chen. Merge commit: feat(rbac): automation tenant bootstrap for private-installer. Closes ENG-1458, ENG-1472.
notes_for_operators: Operator steps: 1) Ensure installer config has enable_rbac_automation=true and (optionally) enable_kms if using KMS-bound service accounts. 2) Run installer in dry-run mode to validate plan. 3) Use --prune-rbac with caution: it can remove bindings not managed by Helm. 4) Audit logs for RBAC changes are written to ${AUDIT_BUCKET} when configured.
